maps.H1_H2_normalisation: H1 = 2 sum_{mu,nu} (d_mu A_nu, [A_mu, A_nu]) (2-form pairing sum_{mu<nu}), H2 = sum_{mu,w} (d_mu iota_w A, [A_mu, iota_w A]); same in theory and engine B

F3.equation: Ob_3 = Q F_3 + {I_3, F_2},  F_3 = unit * sum_j h_j H_j,  F_2 = unit * [ (27/16) int(d^*A|_V, d^*A|_V) + beta_1 int(dA|_V,dA|_V) + beta_2 int(dA|_Wperp,dA|_Wperp) + beta_3 int(lambda,dslash lambda) + beta_4 int(dc,A^*) ]
F3.particular_F3_written_out: unit * [ -(11/8 + (19/8) log(3/2)) int(dA|_V,[A|_V ^ A|_V]) - (11/2 + (19/2) log(3/2)) int([A|_Wperp, c], A^*|_Wperp) - 9 log(3/2) int([c, lambda], lambda^*) ]

representative_with_F3_zero.choice: beta_1 = beta_2 = alpha_1/2 (= alpha_3/2), beta_3 = alpha_5/2, beta_4 = 0, kappa_1 = 0, kappa_2 = -alpha_3
representative_with_F3_zero.F2: unit * [ (27/16) int(d^*A|_V,d^*A|_V) + (11/8 + (19/8) log(3/2)) ( int(dA|_V,dA|_V) + int(dA|_Wperp,dA|_Wperp) ) - (9/2) log(3/2) int(lambda, dslash lambda) ]
representative_with_F3_zero.statement: Ob_3 = {I_3, F_2} exactly: {I_3, int(dA|_V,dA|_V)} = 2 G1, {I_3, int(dA|_Wperp,dA|_Wperp)} = 2 G3, {I_3, int(lambda,dslash lambda)} = 2 G5, {I_3, int(d^*A|_V,d^*A|_V)} = 2 G2; possible because alpha_1 = alpha_3 and alpha_4 = 0. The cubic obstruction is absorbed by finite Q-closed quadratic kinetic counterterms alone (plus the Step-1 (27/16) term).

free_directions.beta_1: F_2 += beta_1 int(dA|_V,dA|_V), F_3 += beta_1 H1  (cubic part of int(F_A,F_A) along V)
free_directions.beta_2: F_2 += beta_2 int(dA|_Wperp,dA|_Wperp), F_3 += 2 beta_2 H2  (cubic part of int(d_A phi, d_A phi))
free_directions.beta_3: F_2 += beta_3 int(lambda,dslash lambda), F_3 += -2 beta_3 H5  (Q-equivalent to the cubic part int(lambda, rho([A,lambda])) of int(lambda, dslash_A lambda))
free_directions.beta_4: F_2 += beta_4 int(dc,A^*), F_3 += beta_4 (H3 + H4 + H5 + H6/2)  (cubic part of the BRST term)
free_directions.kappa_1: F_3 += kappa_1 (H1 - 4 H3 - 2 H6)  (Q-closed, not Q-exact)

F3.agreement_with_engine_B_family: identical (engine B parametrises by h4, h6: kappa_1 = -h6/2 + beta_4/4, kappa_2 = -(h4 + 2 alpha_3 - beta_4)/2)

wess_zumino.statement: Q Ob_3 + {I_3, Ob_2} = (alpha_2 - 27/8) unit Q G2 (Q G1 = Q G3 = Q G4 = Q G5 = 0 on (c,c,A|_V))
wess_zumino.automatic: yes: Q^2 = 0 on lim Q W, Q I_3 = 0, Q Ob_2 = 0, Q P(0,infty) = K_0 and the two limit statements (I-b + III(K_eps-K_0) -> 0, I-d + II-b -> tree(Ob_2, I_3; P(0,infty))); it is not a consequence of linear algebra alone (Q on span H plus the beta-brackets misses G2). Solvability <=> WZ <=> alpha_2 = 27/8, and the computed alpha_2 is 27/8.

master_integrals.method: last [1,oo) integral in closed form (binomial), remaining variables by 40-digit tanh-sinh

notes: Engines A and B are independent codes but share two Step-1 inputs: the cubic log multiples 6, 10, 1, 1, 1 (II-a) and the mass coefficient 9/4 (I-b, III, II-b; recomputed from the graphs by engine A). The II-a and III(K_0) log parts are reproduced here in the theory realisation from Y_3 = 6 AAA + 10 lambda lambda A + AcA^* + c lambda lambda^* + ccc^* and Y_2 = -B1 - B2 + 4 B3 - B4; the III(K_eps-K_0) limit from (9/4){I_3,int(A,HA)}.

Both engines use the same graph decomposition (special edge K_eps - K_0 on the loop, Schwinger times scaled by eps, special time in [0,1], the others in [1,infty)) but different master integrals (engine A: no power of the special time; engine B: J3(a1,a2,a3;m), J2(a1,a2;m)) and different numerator constructions; the master values are confirmed independently here (qa/masters_indep.json).
Finite-eps full-sum numerics: engine A in all four sectors (deviation ~ eps log eps); engine B in (c,c,A^*|_V) (full sum) and (c,A|_Wperp,A|_Wperp) (I-a only).
log(3/2) enters alpha_1 = alpha_3 and alpha_5 only; these coefficients are not constrained by the Wess-Zumino condition and are removed by the finite counterterm (scheme constants).
